title: 31 ##### 1.6.13 Districtwise Crime Districts in India which registered more than 5,000 cognizable offences under the Indian Penal Code in 1979 were Chingalput East, South Arcot, Thanjavur West, Tiruchirapalli, Tirunelveli, Salem and North Arcot in Tamil Nadu, East Godavari, Krishna and Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, Thane, Nasik, Akola, Amravati, Pune City and Nagpur City in Maharashtra, Mehsana and Kaira in Gujarat; Gwalior, Indore, Ujjain, Jabalpur, Raipur, Bilaspur, Bhopal and Durg in Madhya Pradesh, Jaipur in Rajasthan, North, Central, West and South Districts of Delhi, Meerut, Bulandshahr, Ghaziabad, Aligarh, Agra, Kanpur, Allahabad, Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Bareilly, Moradabad, and Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, Patna and Purnea in Bihar, Cuttack and Sambalpur in Orissa, Burdwan, Hooghly, 24-Parganas, Nadia, Howrah and Midnapore in West Bengal and Kamrup, Sibsagar and Cachar in Assam. The hill districts of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Sikkim and the North Eastern region had very low incidence of crime.
